papers.title: HPV6/11 Persistence and Treatment-Associated Immune Remodeling in Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis: A Cross-Cohort Transcriptomic Analysis.
papers.abstract: Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), caused mainly by human papillomavirus types 6 and 11 (HPV6/11), can persist despite the absence of recognized systemic immunodeficiency. We reanalyzed three transcriptomic datasets using the same predefined immune-gene programs: paired papilloma and autologous laryngeal mucosa from 12 patients, single-cell RNA sequencing from papillomas of four RRP donors and pharyngopalatine mucosa from three controls, and paired papilloma samples from 17 patients before and after INO-3107, a DNA immunotherapy encoding HPV6/11 antigens and interleukin-12. In untreated tissue, cluster of differentiation 8 (CD8)- and natural killer (NK)-associated cytotoxic program scores were lower and the transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) suppressive program score was higher, reproducing findings from the same cohort. The lower cytotoxic pattern was not reproduced within the recovered combined T-cell and NK-cell population, although no single-cell comparison remained significant after correction for multiple testing. After INO-3107, CD8- and NK-associated cytotoxic, T helper 1 (Th1)/interferon gamma (IFN-γ), and C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3 (CXCR3)-associated trafficking program scores increased significantly, whereas TGF-β and M2-like suppressive programs showed no comparable statistically supported change. Together, these findings show that different components of the local immune response do not change in parallel and support a model of selective treatment-associated immune remodeling. This pattern may inform future biomarker and combination-treatment studies.

papers.title: Tissue Factor Expression Is Associated with Distinct Pattern of Immune-Cell Infiltration in the Ovarian Tumor Microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Tissue factor (TF) has been implicated in tumor progression and immune regulation, but its cellular sources and relationship with immune infiltration in ovarian cancer remain incompletely defined. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE232314), analyses of The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) ovarian cancer cohort, and multiplex immunofluorescence in an independent 25-case tissue microarray (TMA). Single-cell analysis showed that TF expression was concentrated in tumor epithelial cells and a discrete endothelial subpopulation, with minimal expression in immune and other stromal compartments. In the TCGA cohort, TF expression was not significantly associated with tumor stage, grade, disease-free survival, or overall survival. In TF-stratified analyses, however, high CD8+ T cell infiltration was associated with improved survival in the low-TF expression subgroup (HR = 0.60) but with worse survival in the high-TF subgroup (HR = 1.72); high M1 macrophage infiltration was associated with improved survival only in the low-TF subgroup. TF expression correlated negatively with estimated CD8+ T cell, memory B cell, and M1 macrophage infiltration and positively with naïve B cell infiltration. In the TMA cohort, high-TF tumors showed significantly lower CD56+ NK-cell and CD68+ macrophage infiltration and a lower CD68/CD163 ratio. Together, these findings show cross-sectional associations between TF expression and reduced measured abundance of several antitumor immune populations and a stratum-dependent association between CD8+ T cell infiltration and survival. These associations were not fully concordant between the transcriptomic (TCGA) and protein-level (TMA) cohorts and require prospective, formally tested validation. TF warrants further investigation as a candidate immune-context biomarker in ovarian cancer.

papers.title: Metabolic reprogramming of NK cells in chronic brucellar arthritis: role of the HIF-1α/mTOR axis.
papers.abstract:
Brucellar arthritis is the most common complication of brucellosis, and its chronic progression is closely associated with immune cell dysfunction. Natural killer (NK) cells play a central role in anti-infective immunity; however, their functional status and regulatory mechanisms in brucellar arthritis remain poorly understood.
Peripheral blood and synovial tissue samples were collected from healthy controls, as well as from patients with acute-phase and chronic-phase brucellar arthritis. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), flow cytometry, quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR), JC-1 mitochondrial membrane potential assay, Seahorse metabolic analysis, and Western blotting were employed to systematically evaluate NK cell phenotypes, functions, metabolic profiles, and HIF-1α/mTOR pathway activity. In vitro, heat-killed Brucella melitensis 16M (HKBA) was used to stimulate NK-92 cells and HIF-1α-knockout (KO) cell lines, with mTOR inhibitor intervention, to dissect the regulatory mechanism of the HIF-1α/mTOR axis in NK cell metabolic reprogramming.
scRNA-seq revealed enrichment of NK cells in the synovium of brucellar arthritis patients, with aberrant expression of oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS)-related genes. Clinical sample analyses showed that, compared with healthy controls, the proportion of peripheral blood NK cells increased in both acute- and chronic-phase patients; however, NK cells from chronic-phase patients exhibited significantly reduced IFN-γ, Granzyme B, and CD107a degranulation levels. HIF-1α protein was consistently overexpressed in patient NK cells, whereas phosphorylated mTOR-pathway proteins (p-PI3K, p-AKT, p-mTOR) were markedly suppressed. In vitro, HKBA treatment inhibited mTOR pathway activity in NK-92 cells in a dose- and time-dependent manner and reduced mitochondrial membrane potential as shown by JC-1 staining. HIF-1α knockout significantly restored NK cell cytotoxic function, upregulated OXPHOS- and glycolysis-related gene expression, and improved mitochondrial membrane potential. Transcriptomic sequencing confirmed enrichment of mTOR signaling and energy metabolism gene sets after knockout. Importantly, mTOR pathway inhibition completely blocked the HIF-1α-knockout-mediated restoration of NK cell function and mitochondrial fitness, indicating that HIF-1α primarily drives NK cell metabolic and functional abnormalities through mTOR suppression.
Brucella infection induces HIF-1α overexpression, which suppresses mTOR signaling and drives metabolic reprogramming of NK cells characterized by impaired OXPHOS and functional exhaustion, thereby promoting chronicity of brucellar arthritis. Targeting the HIF-1α/mTOR axis may offer a novel therapeutic strategy for brucellar arthritis.

papers.title: Female hormones enhance skin T cell expansion and suppress IFN-γ production.
papers.abstract:
Estrogen receptors (ERs) regulate immune function, but their expression across immune cell subsets and hormone responsiveness in human skin are not fully understood.
We used 10-color flow cytometry to quantify ER (ERα, ERβ, and GPER1) expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy donors. We analyzed sex hormone gene expression using public single-cell RNA datasets. Skin immune responses to sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS) were assessed in pre- and post-menopausal women, with or without hormone replacement therapy (HRT). Furthermore, we measured the production of mediators in the ER expressing immune cytotoxic cells, specifically T and NK cells, in response to pre- and post-menopausal hormone cocktails.
ERα was predominantly expressed on the membrane of NK and NKT cells, while ERβ was mainly intracellular and showed low expression across subsets. GPER1 displayed a similar membrane distribution to ERα but at lower expression levels. T cells displayed moderate membrane ERα and lower GPER1 expression. Gene expression analysis in women revealed strong ESR1 and ESR2 expression in T cells. In inflamed skin, HRT selectively increased T cell numbers after SLS exposure in post-menopausal women. In vitro, female hormones dose-dependently decreased IFN-γ production in T and NK cells but did not alter cytotoxic mediator production in these cells.
ER expression levels and localization vary by immune cell subset, indicating that estrogen modulates immune responses in a cell-specific manner. Sex hormones differentially impact T and NK cell populations during skin inflammation, by increasing T cell numbers and, reducing IFN-γ, without altering cytotoxic activity. These findings demonstrate that female sex hormones significantly influence immune responses in inflamed and aging skin and may guide the development of targeted therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Osteoclast-Expanded Natural Killer Cells Are a Unique Population of Cells Based on Transcriptomic and Single-Cell RNA-Sequencing and Proteomic and Functional Characteristics.
papers.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells, known for their potent anti-tumor activity, have faced challenges in clinical trials due to limited methods to enhance their expansion and anti-tumor potential. This review highlights the unique characteristics of osteoclasts-expanded supercharged NK (sNK) cells, showcasing their suitability for clinical applications. sNK cells exhibit remarkable anti-tumor efficacy, prolonged survival, and increased expansion when cultured with osteoclasts and probiotic bacteria. A comparative analysis with other NK cell expansion techniques reveals the distinct advantages of sNK cells in terms of survival, expansion, and functionality. Through proteomic, transcriptomic, single-cell RNAseq, and functional assessments, sNK cells demonstrate the ability to target both poorly differentiated/stem-like tumors and well-differentiated tumors. Moreover, they can supplement the functional deficiency of autologous NK cells, restoring their effectiveness in combating cancer. The exceptional attributes of sNK cells position them as a unique and promising candidate for inclusion in clinical trials for cancer patients.
